title: Admin Conductor: Priority Lane for Emergency Shortflows
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: oncall engineers currently run a mix of ad-hoc scripts and monolithic runbooks during high-severity incidents. This leads to inconsistent latencies, unclear audit trails, and variable safety guarantees. We need a thin 'priority lane' in the Admin Conductor that converts vetted emergency runbook fragments into atomic, pre-authorized tasklets that can be executed with a single click and strong telemetry.

Scope: build a runtime path and orchestration policy that (1) identifies emergency shortflows (<= 5 steps) from the runbook registry, (2) compiles them into tasklets with typed inputs and explicit undo checkpoints, (3) exposes a guarded execution API surfaced in the ops console and CLI, and (4) streams rich per-step telemetry for post-incident analysis. This ticket covers infra + runtime + rollout gating for the priority lane only; conversion tooling for the broader library will be follow-ups.

Goals:
- Reduce median time to remediate for P0/P1 operational issues by 30% when using priority lane tasklets.
- Ensure each tasklet has an automatic undo or safe-fail path and RBAC gating.
- Emit per-step tracing and cost metrics to the ops telemetry pipeline so every execution is auditable and searchable.

Non-goals: full migration of all runbooks, replacing manual runbook authoring UX, or modifying customer-facing behavior outside of internal remediation flows.
acceptance_criteria: Priority lane can register and run a shortflow tasklet with typed inputs via API and console
All executed tasklets produce per-step traces in the ops telemetry stream within 5s of step completion
Tasklets include a configurable undo token or idempotent safe-fail strategy
RBAC checks occur at launch time and are logged to audit with user and session metadata
Canary rollout documented and tested (10% of oncall rotations) with rollback plan
comments: 2026-02-21 -- Kickoff: synced with PM, Design and SRE. Agreed to prioritize shortflows first; longflows deferred to ENG-XXXXX follow-up.

2026-02-27 -- Design review: UX for console button and confirmation modal accepted by Design (see Confluence doc). Remaining concern: too many confirmations will slow remediation; decided to add a single 'requires justification' field for sensitive tasklets.

2026-03-02 -- Architecture review: two runtime options proposed: (A) embed in existing Admin Conductor service (faster), (B) new lightweight runner service with strict sandboxing (safer). Team voted for option B gated by performance bench milestone.

2026-03-05 -- Prototype: implemented tasklet compilation pipeline and a first-pass sandbox runner. End-to-end demo against synthetic shortflow done. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/admin-conductor/pull/314 (WIP)

2026-03-08 -- SRE safety review: requested explicit undo token patterns and rate-limits. Added a preflight dry-run flag and quota checks. Security suggested HSM-backed signing for high-sensitivity commands; ticketed as follow-up (ENG-982000).
2026-03-10 -- QA: integration tests for RBAC and trace emission added. Need to add cost-accounting tag enrichment before canary rollout.
